title: Asbestos Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1101)
subtitle: Use before asbestos work begins and at each shift on construction, renovation, maintenance or demolition jobs.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only where the item's work class or control method does not apply to the job.
Report any Defect to the competent person, who has authority to take prompt corrective measures, and recheck the item before work resumes.
The manufacturer's instructions for enclosures, glovebags and respirators, and your site rules, may add checks.

sections.title: Before work starts
items: Each task recorded as Class I, II, III or IV using the definitions; TSI and surfacing material treated as PACM unless rebutted
Assessment done by the competent person immediately before or at the start of the operation, before exposure-dependent controls are chosen
A competent person is assigned to and supervising the asbestos work inside the regulated area
Other employers on site have been told about the asbestos work, the regulated area rules and how their employees are protected
Flooring, mastic and backing handled as asbestos-containing unless an industrial hygienist has determined it asbestos-free
A written respiratory protection program meeting the listed parts of 1910.134 covers every employee who must wear a respirator

sections.title: Regulated area and isolation
items: Boundary clearly marked (barriers or enclosure may serve) and signs displayed
Only authorized persons inside the boundary
No food, drink, smoking, chewing tobacco or gum, or cosmetics inside the boundary
Everyone entering where respirators are required has one selected under (h)(3)
Critical barriers in place, or an alternative isolation method verified by perimeter surveillance and monitoring, wherever (g)(4)(ii) applies
HVAC openings sealed with a double layer of 6 mil plastic or equivalent
Impermeable dropcloths laid beneath all removal activity
Objects inside covered with impermeable dropcloths or plastic sheeting secured by duct tape or equivalent
Manometer shows at least −0.02 column inches of water differential relative to outside, held throughout use
Enclosure inspected for breaches and smoke-tested before work and at each shift start; any leaks sealed

sections.title: Work practices and controls
items: HEPA-filtered vacuums used to collect all ACM and PACM dust and debris
Material kept wet during handling, removal, cutting and cleanup, unless the employer can demonstrate wetting is infeasible
Waste and debris picked up promptly and placed in leak-tight containers
No high-speed abrasive disc saw in use without a point-of-cut ventilator or HEPA-exhausted enclosure
No compressed air used to remove asbestos unless with an enclosed system capturing the dust cloud
No dry sweeping, shoveling or other dry cleanup of ACM or PACM debris
Exposure is not being managed by rotating workers in and out
Each glovebag smoke-tested and leaks sealed before use
Each glovebag used once and not moved along the pipe
Roof ACM carried, passed down by hand, or lowered by covered chute, crane or hoist; never dropped or thrown

sections.title: Monitoring, PPE and adjacent areas
items: Daily sampling representative of each employee doing Class I or II work in the regulated area, unless an NEA covers the whole operation or the (f)(3)(iii) exception applies
Employees notified within 5 working days of results being received, in writing or by accessible posting
Monitoring restarted after any change in process, controls, personnel or work practices that may raise exposure
Affected employees and their representatives offered the chance to observe exposure monitoring
No filtering facepiece respirators worn for asbestos
Powered and non-powered air-purifying respirators fitted with HEPA filters
Coveralls or similar, head and foot coverings and gloves worn where exposure exceeds a PEL, a required NEA is missing, or large Class I TSI or surfacing removal is under way
Contaminated clothing laundered in a way that prevents airborne asbestos release above the PELs
Employers next to another contractor's regulated area check enclosure integrity or control effectiveness every day

references: 29 CFR 1926.1101: Asbestos (Part 1926 Subpart Z, Toxic and Hazardous Substances)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
